assumptions: Power is computed from per-unit-normalized attributes (R5-01): each attribute is classified into a unit group (combat_power, survivability, mobility, utility) and normalized to [0,1] within its group across the object set, so incomparable units are not silently summed at different raw scales.
Weights are unit-group-aware: combat_power > survivability > mobility > utility, normalized to sum to 1.
Nash equilibrium for 2×2 zero-sum games is computed via the closed-form formula p* = (d-c)/(a-b-c+d) (R5-04). For larger matrices, falls back to uniform-over-non-dominated with source='heuristic'.
The nash_method and nash_source fields distinguish real solver results from the heuristic fallback.
Synergy is a deterministic name-hash proxy, not an interaction simulation.
Win rates come from repeated RNG trials over the synthetic payoff model.
The payoff model is not an executable gameplay model.
Stability is measured over generated resource-flow trials with fixed synthetic rules.
Overall stability aggregates synthetic balance diagnostics and is not a playtest score.
Composite score (R5-08): stability - transitive OP/UP penalty - intransitive dominance penalty - Monte Carlo verdict penalty, with a hard gate capping score at 0.3 when critical issues exist.
Before R5-08 this was just stability.overall_stability, which ignored OP/UP, dominance and MC verdict.
